To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intrahepatically produced immunosuppressive mediators are involved in the control of the immune response against viral infection and that KC and LSEC may play a critical role in the control of NK and NKT cells.
viral tropism of KC and LEC is involved in immunosurveillance disorders during acute viral hepatitis.
viral tropism for KC and LSEC in viral hepatitis may be involved in the decrease in immunosuppression and NK/NK T cell disorders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the roles of KC and LESC in the disturbances of intrahepatics immunosuppressive mechanisms during acute viral hepatitis.
the role of intrahepatical KC and LSEC in the disturbances of the immune tolerance during viral acute hepatitis.
the role of intrahepatically produced immunosuppressive factors in the disturbances of the NK/NKT cells, NK T cells and regulatory T cells during acute viral liver injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the balance between immunosuppressive and proinflammatory cytokines is altered in the liver during acute viral hepatitis and this may be due to the permissive nature of KC and LEC to viral infection.
the permissivity of the KC and LSEC to MHV3 infection, and the subsequent production of cytokines, may contribute to the disorders of immune tolerance and NK cell apoptosis in viral hepatitis.
KC and LSEC are involved in the disturbances of the intrahepatically sustained immunosuppression and the NK/NK T cell disorder, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intrahepatically infected KC and LSEC are involved in immunosubversion and NK T cell apoptosis during acute viral hepatitis.

the viral permissivity for LSEC and KC may contribute to the decrease of intrahepatically produced immunosuppressive factors and apoptosis of intrahepatical NK and NK  T cells, resulting in an increased NK cell‐mediated cytotoxicity and a decrease in immunosuppression during acute viral hepatitis.
the viral tropism of KC and LESC is involved in immunological disorders during viral hepatitis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the intrahepatically infected Kupffer and LSEC cells are involved in the immunopathological events of acute viral hepatitis.
the intrahepital tolerance may be disturbed by the permissivity of liver sinusoidal endothelium (LSEC) and Kupffer cells (CK) during acute hepatitis.
the permissiveness of KC and LESC to viral replication is involved in the disturbances of intrahepatics immune tolerance during viral acute hepatitis.
